decisive_items: prolonged PTT of 49 s with normal PT/INR/fibrinogen
response.rationale: SLE is the unifying autoimmune diagnosis: malar rash, inflammatory symmetric wrist stiffness, cytopenias, serositis, and lupus anticoagulant with recurrent thrombosis/miscarriage explain the tricuspid vegetations (Libman-Sacks/NBTE) and APS features. NBTE and APS are complications/associations, not the primary systemic diagnosis; RHD lacks supporting history.

rejected.why: NBTE is the valvular lesion but is secondary to the underlying SLE/APS; it does not explain malar rash, wrist stiffness, or cytopenias.
APS explains thrombosis, miscarriage, and prolonged PTT but not the SLE-defining mucocutaneous and articular features; it is a complication of SLE.
No history of rheumatic fever; tricuspid vegetations with negative cultures and SLE features make rheumatic heart disease unlikely.
